claims.text: Wound prep before closure: keep betadine, peroxide and chlorhexidine out of the wound.
claims.quote: keep betadine, peroxide, chlorhexidine OUT of the wound

claims.text: Lidocaine is the go-to anesthetic, injected into the wound and its edges.
claims.quote: Lidocaine = the “go-to” - injected directly into wound + wound edges

claims.text: Primary intention: approximate all layers with sutures, staples, adhesive or steri-strips.
claims.quote: 1° intention: approximate ALL tissue layers - little/no tissue loss - minimal scarring - sutures, staples, skin adhesives, steri-strips

claims.text: Simple interrupted sutures suit most wounds.
claims.quote: Simple interrupted: + simple - majority of wounds

claims.text: Hair apposition (HAT) for scalp wounds: twist hair from each side together and glue. Good for kids, no needle.
claims.quote: HAT (hair apposition technique): literature since 2002 - intact hair from opposite sides of scalp wound - pull together, twist + glue - hair length dictates feasibility - GREAT for kids, no needle

claims.text: Tissue adhesive: fast, no anesthesia, nothing to remove.
claims.quote: Tissue adhesives: + fast - no anesthesia - no removal - minimal additional inflammation

claims.text: Tetanus: after the full childhood series, boost if > 5 years for a tetanus-prone wound, > 10 years for a low-risk one.
claims.quote: completed childhood series (5 doses) → booster if >5 yr since last immunization w tetanus-prone wound; >10 yr if low-risk wound

claims.text: Recheck the wound in 24 to 48 hours.
